# NGSentinel QC decision rules
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each rule compares one metric with two thresholds.
#   direction: higher  -> PASS if value >= pass, REVIEW if value >= review, else FAIL
#   direction: lower   -> PASS if value <= pass, REVIEW if value <= review, else FAIL
# Metric paths:  before.<summary key>, after.<summary key>, trimming.<key>
# These defaults are general starting points for short-read Illumina data, NOT
# universal standards: adjust them to your assay (e.g. amplicon or RNA-seq
# libraries legitimately show high duplication). Research use only.
version: 1
rules:
  - id: q30
    metric: after.q30_pct
    label: Bases with quality >= Q30 (after preprocessing)
    direction: higher
    pass: 80
    review: 70
    unit: "%"
    rationale: >-
      Q30 means an estimated base-call error rate of 1 in 1,000. A low Q30 fraction
      increases the number of sequencing errors carried into alignment and variant calling.

  - id: mean_quality
    metric: after.mean_quality
    label: Mean base quality (after preprocessing)
    direction: higher
    pass: 30
    review: 25
    unit: " Phred"
    rationale: >-
      The average Phred score summarises base-call confidence across all retained bases.

  - id: adapter
    metric: after.adapter_max_pct
    label: Residual adapter content (after preprocessing)
    direction: lower
    pass: 1
    review: 5
    unit: "%"
    rationale: >-
      Adapter sequence left in reads does not originate from the sample and can cause
      mis-alignment and false variants. FastQC warns above 5 % and fails above 10 %.

  - id: retention
    metric: trimming.retention_pct
    label: Read retention after preprocessing
    direction: higher
    pass: 90
    review: 70
    unit: "%"
    rationale: >-
      Shows the cost of cleaning: a large loss of reads can indicate a poor library or
      overly strict trimming parameters, and reduces usable depth.

  - id: duplication
    metric: after.duplication_pct
    label: Duplicate reads (sampled, after preprocessing)
    direction: lower
    pass: 30
    review: 50
    unit: "%"
    rationale: >-
      High duplication can indicate PCR over-amplification or low library complexity.
      Expected to be high for amplicon, small-RNA and highly expressed RNA-seq libraries.

  - id: n_content
    metric: after.n_pct
    label: Undetermined bases (N)
    direction: lower
    pass: 0.1
    review: 1
    unit: "%"
    rationale: >-
      N bases are positions the sequencer could not call; a high fraction indicates
      instrument or cluster problems.

  - id: gc_deviation
    metric: after.gc_deviation_pct
    label: GC distribution deviation from normal
    direction: lower
    pass: 15
    review: 30
    unit: "%"
    rationale: >-
      A per-read GC distribution that departs from a normal shape can indicate
      contamination or a biased library (FastQC thresholds: warn 15 %, fail 30 %).

  - id: read_count
    metric: after.total_reads
    label: Reads remaining after preprocessing
    direction: higher
    pass: 10000
    review: 1000
    unit: " reads"
    rationale: >-
      Too few reads limit statistical power. Set this to the depth your experiment needs.
